artifacts.summary: Transcribes the chapter-quality standard's 15 dual-tagged rules, maps the typst-element-lint.sh structural precedent onto chapter-quality-check.sh, names the six wiring sites and their exact element-lint analogs, and flags two open risks (bib/repo-root resolution for Rules 1.2/1.3, and deploy verification since the typst extension is not currently active in this repo).

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system, an extension's own standard file can define an 'Interface Contract for Repo-Local Checks' section that names checks a *consuming repository* must implement locally (never duplicated by the extension's own mechanical checker), while still requiring the extension's checker to implement other, superficially similar rules directly (e.g. path-existence and citation-key resolution). When transcribing such a standard into a checker script, explicitly separate 'rules this checker owns' from 'checks explicitly deferred to a consumer' in the script's own header comment, or the two categories get conflated during implementation.

deploy-headless.sh's default (non---wipe) mode only force-resyncs extensions already marked active in a repo's .claude-extensions.json (plus core unconditionally); it will NOT deploy an extension that has never been loaded into that repo. To verify a not-yet-active extension's manifest/index wiring actually deploys correctly, use the scratch-git-repo pattern already proven by scripts/tests/test-deploy-propagation.sh (a mktemp -d throwaway target + the real deploy-headless.sh + the real Lua manager.load engine) rather than attempting to load the extension permanently into the working repo's own .claude-extensions.json.
